entries.comment: Prime 4: The Viewros incident (Metroid Prime 4: Beyond events)
entries.content:
In Cosmic Year 20X9 the bounty hunter Sylux and a Space Pirate army under his command were raiding Galactic Federation research facilities. The Pirates were believed to be controlled by a new strain of Metroid able to fuse with other life-forms and seize their minds. When the UTO Research Center on Tanamaar, in the Desolan System, came under attack, Federation HQ dispatched Samus Aran, who was nearby on reconnaissance, to secure a recently unearthed alien artifact that analysis had identified only as some kind of device (Metroid Prime 4: Beyond).

Samus fought through the breached facility while its staff rushed the artifact to the hangar. There a Metroid fused with Aberax, a giant Space Pirate officer, and Samus destroyed it before Sylux broke in with more Pirates and Metroids. During their duel Sylux damaged the artifact; it activated and engulfed the center in an energy burst that flung Samus, Sylux, several Federation personnel and parts of the facility to Viewros, a planet on no known star chart, lying beyond time and space.

Samus woke inside the Chrono Tower with most of her suit's capabilities gone. A Lamorn Guardian mechanoid led her to the Psychic Crystal, which awakened psychic abilities in her, and at the tower's Pinnacle a recorded message from Chatoyant Vooloon, last priest of the extinct Lamorn, named her the Chosen One foretold to carry the Lamorn legacy to a new world. The Master Teleporter at the Pinnacle could send her home, but only after the five Master Teleporter Keys entrusted to Guardians across Viewros were recovered. The Lamorn also asked her to ripen the Memory Fruit of the Sacred Tree by feeding it Green Energy from crystals scattered over the planet.

In the jungle of Fury Green Samus rescued the Federation engineer Myles MacKenzie, who became her voice on comms and set up a Base Camp. Riding the Lamorn vehicle Vi-O-La across the desert hub of Sol Valley, she took the keys from Fury Green, Volt Forge, Ice Belt, Flare Pool and the Great Mines and found the other stranded Federation personnel: the sniper Reger Tokabi, Sergeant Ezra Duke, Private First Class Nora Armstrong and the combat android VUE-995. Lamorn records revealed that Green Energy, meant to heal the planet, had driven its wildlife savage and transformed the Lamorn themselves into the feral Grievers. Sylux, gravely hurt on arrival, had healed inside the Chrono Tower, sealed it behind a barrier, sent Psy-bot Mimics in his likeness against Samus and infused his Metroids into the key Guardians.

MacKenzie's rebuilt Federation mech Betsy breached the barrier. At the Pinnacle Sylux, transformed by the tower's energies, ambushed the group, dragged Samus through a dimensional rift and was beaten by her in the void beyond. As she activated the Master Teleporter he returned and damaged it so that it could hold only moments, and it answered only to Samus. The five Federation soldiers seized Sylux and held him down, telling her to go. She teleported away alone. On a barren world she planted the Memory Fruit together with her Psychic Crystal; a tree sprang up at once, her white Lamorn Legacy Suit faded back to the Varia Suit, and she hung Reger Tokabi's tag on its branches in tribute to the companions she had left behind. Their fate, and Sylux's, remain unknown.
entries.notes: Release date verified as December 4, 2025 (Metroid Wiki, Wikipedia). Cosmic Year 20X9, Desolan System and 'nearby on reconnaissance' come from the in-game opening text (Metroid Wiki summary + Shinesparkers transcript). 'Could hold only moments' and 'answered only to Samus' are from the GameSpot ending piece (single outlet; the fan wiki adds that only someone with psychic abilities can activate it). Samus's suit loss being caused by the artifact is TV Tropes-only; content just says she woke with most capabilities gone (multiple guides). Destination world after the teleport is unconfirmed (some sources guess Tanamaar); left unnamed. 'Legacy Suit' name is from a Retro Studios interview and guides, not a wiki page.

entries.content:
Sylux is a human bounty hunter, said to come from the planet Cylosis, who wears a blue armored suit and excels at stealth, tracking and marksmanship. He harbors an intense hatred for the Galactic Federation and for Samus Aran, whom he despises for serving it (per the Metroid Prime Hunters manual).

Equipment:
- Shock Coil: banned technology that fires charged blasts of high-density neutrinos as a continuous beam of blue lightning, draining an opponent's energy and feeding it to Sylux.
- Lockjaw: his alternate form, two tetracarbon ceramic-alloy blades joined by an energy thread, faster than a Morph Ball; it lays up to three bombs linked by trip wires. On Viewros it could also shield him from gunfire, ram Samus to tear an Energy Tank from her, and stun with an electric rush.
- Delano 7: a Delta-class gunship, blue with green accents, with an automatic cannon on its lower hull. Like his suit and weapons it is believed to be stolen Federation prototype technology.

Career:
- Alimbic Cluster incident (Metroid Prime Hunters): after attacking a Federation vessel on a snowy world he followed Samus to the Alimbic Cluster seeking the ultimate power. Samus first met him at the Vesper Defense Outpost; Delano 7 supported him in battle. She saved him from Gorea, yet he fled with his hatred intact.
- After the Phazon crisis, Delano 7 was seen shadowing Samus's gunship as she departed.
- Bermuda System incident: he broke into a Federation research station and hatched the Metroid Egg the Federation Force had recovered.

The Viewros incident: exploiting the hatchling's imprinting, Sylux cloned it and bred a Metroid strain that merges with and controls other organisms. With these he seized the minds of Space Pirate officers, took command of their army, upgraded his battlesuit with the latest nanosuit and raided Federation research centers, ending in the attack on Tanamaar. His duel with Samus damaged the Lamorn artifact that hurled both of them to Viewros. Gravely injured, he was carried into the Chrono Tower, where a Lamorn healing pod mended him and synchronized his mind with the tower; he learned of the Lamorn, the Master Teleporter and its five keys. While recovering he sent Psy-bot Mimics, machines indistinguishable from him until destroyed, to attack Samus and seize the keys, infused his Metroids into the keys' Guardians, and sealed the tower behind a barrier. His consciousness brushed Samus's, and she relived his memories as psychic flashbacks. When she reached the Pinnacle he rose from the pod changed, wielding tentacle-like nano-arms and Lamorn energy, tore open a dimensional rift and dragged her through; she beat him in the void beyond, where his Lockjaw could even summon a black hole. Seemingly destroyed, he returned as Samus activated the Master Teleporter and damaged it; the five Federation soldiers held him down while she escaped. He remains on Viewros, still commanding his Metroids and Pirates, his showdown with Samus unresolved.

His past: Sylux was a Federation officer in command of a squad fighting the Space Pirates. Ordered to hold position until Samus's team arrived, he disobeyed ("Get me that weapon") to seize a Pirate superweapon. It annihilated his squad and the Federation mechs with it; he alone survived, barely. Samus arrived in her gunship, destroyed the weapon with ease and offered him her hand, which he slapped away. Blaming her and the Federation, he deserted with stolen prototype gear and became a bounty hunter bent on revenge. Samus now regards him as an enemy who will not go away.
entries.notes: Cylosis origin and 'human' per Metroid Wiki (Hunters-era materials). Nanosuit, imprinting and Pirate-officer control come from Nintendo Today app text as reported by Nintendo World Report, corroborated by the in-game Sylux logbook summary (cloned a stolen Metroid, used clones to control minds, took over the Pirates). Healing pod, 'seize the keys', mind-link flashbacks and 'unavoidable enemy' are from the Tanabe Nintendo Dream interview (Omega Metroid translation). Nintendo Life alone says he 'shoots her in the head' on his return; omitted. Flashback shows Samus's Prime 3-era gunship and Project Golem mechs, which fan analysis notes conflicts with a pre-Hunters origin; not addressed in content. His rank is given as 'field captain' only by Wikipedia (flagged there as needing a better source), so content says 'officer in command of a squad'.

entries.content:
Viewros is an uncharted planet on no known Federation star chart, lying beyond time and space, to which Samus Aran, Sylux and a handful of Federation personnel were hurled when a Lamorn artifact on Tanamaar activated (Metroid Prime 4: Beyond). It was the home of the Lamorn, a psychic civilization now extinct; their ruins, statues and machines cover its surface, and the Grievers, the mutated remnant of their people, dominate its wildlife. Green Energy, once showered over the land by the Lamorn, has left many creatures swollen and aggressive.

Regions:
- Sol Valley: a sun-scorched desert at the planet's heart, the hub from which the other regions branch. The Chrono Tower floats above it; Lamorn shrines and statues conceal underground chambers. Samus crossed it on the Vi-O-La.
- Fury Green: an ancient jungle holding the Temple of Memory and the Sacred Tree, where the Lamorn stored their memories, and the Garden of Remembrance. Myles MacKenzie's Base Camp was set up here, and a Lamorn cargo launcher links it to Sol Valley. The Guardian Carvex held its key.
- Volt Forge: a vehicle factory powered by the planet's lightning storms and run by Xelios, an artificial intelligence grown from organic cells. The Vi-O-La was prototyped and tested here.
- Ice Belt: a frozen research facility built after the Great Tragedy, where Lamorn scientists tried and failed to cure the Grievers; cryopods of frozen Grievers still line its halls. Snow Wolves hunt outside, and the Guardian Keratos held its key.
- Flare Pool: a volcano facility that extracted Green Energy from magma and loaded it into shells fired over Sol Valley. The Guardian Phenoros dwells in its lava lake.
- Great Mines: the Lamorn mineral network where the Viewros Crystal, source of their psychic power, was discovered; now the hunting ground of the Maul Grievers and the Omega Griever.
- Chrono Tower: the floating sanctuary above Sol Valley housing the Master Teleporter.

Samus woke on Viewros stripped of most of her suit's capabilities and left it alone through the Master Teleporter; the five Federation soldiers who held Sylux back remain there, as does Sylux himself. She knows the planet as the place where she gained psychic abilities, lost her companions, and inherited the legacy of a dead people.
entries.notes: Metroid Wiki lists five areas (Fury Green, Sol Valley, Volt Forge, Ice Belt, Flare Pool); the Great Mines and Chrono Tower are confirmed by multiple walkthroughs and the in-game logbook. Region purposes come from Nintendo's Japanese website as machine-translated by Omega Metroid, cross-checked against logbook summaries. 'Another dimension / beyond time and space' is from Tanabe's interview; the in-game line is MacKenzie's 'doesn't appear on any of the known star charts'. 'Garden of Remembrance' is a single-guide room name.

entries.content:
The Lamorn were a peaceful, graceful and deeply spiritual species of high intelligence that inhabited Viewros and are now extinct. Robed, with aquatic features and no visible mouth, they communicated telepathically; Samus Aran can understand their recorded speech. A priesthood stood at the center of their culture, and while every Lamorn could manipulate psychic energy, the priests mastered it. When they first arrived on Viewros they planted the Sacred Tree, which holds the memories and knowledge of their whole people; Lamorn prayed at the altar of the Temple of Memory in Fury Green and their memories passed into the tree, which bears them as Memory Fruit.

History: in their Machine Era the Lamorn built the Great Mines, the Volt Forge factory, hover shuttles, Scout Bots and the Vi-O-La, until resources ran short. The discovery of the Viewros Crystal in the mines began the Psychic Era: a rare few were born with a circular crystal in the forehead that granted psychic and telepathic power, and processed crystals were implanted in the rest. Revered priests included Thesarh, the first priest, who communed with the Sacred Tree and founded the Temple of Memory; Shei, the only female priest, whose grasp of space and time led to the teleporter; Lekhash, the sculptor-mathematician whose equations became psychic objects, including the sealing mechanism of the Master Teleporter and its keys; and Vahkuun, inventor of the Mote-operated Psychic Lock and builder of the shrines of Sol Valley.

The Great Tragedy: seeking to restore a planet damaged by their industry, the Lamorn extracted Green Energy, a seemingly limitless fuel, from the magma of Flare Pool and fired it over Sol Valley in showers that revived flora and fauna. Overexposure reacted with the implanted crystals and twisted those Lamorn into the feral Grievers, who hunted the rest. Survivors under the priest Chatoya ran laboratories in the Ice Belt trying to reverse the change with refined Green Energy; every attempt failed, and the researcher Tahrgun's last log reads, "I am Tahrgun. And I am utterly defeated." The final thirteen Lamorn withdrew to the Chrono Tower in Sol Valley. Twelve departed through small return teleporters to other worlds to search for a prophesied Chosen One, and each died where they landed; one came to rest on Tanamaar, where the Galactic Federation later dug up its teleporter. Chatoyant Vooloon, called Chatoya, stayed behind and left recordings to set the Chosen One on the path: gather the five Master Teleporter Keys, feed Green Energy to the Memory Fruit, and carry it to a new world. Their last gift to the Chosen One was the Legacy Suit, a white suit that wraps its wearer in a defensive barrier.

Samus fulfilled that charge. The Lamorn recordings addressed her as the Chosen One, and after escaping Viewros she planted the Memory Fruit on another world, giving up the Legacy Suit as it took root.
entries.notes: Priest names (Thesarh, Shei, Lekhash, Vahkuun) and Tahrgun's logs come from the in-game Lamorn Legacy logbook as transcribed by Omega Metroid (single transcription source, but primary text). Thirteen survivors / twelve searchers / one on Tanamaar: Shinesparkers feature and Tanabe interview agree. Legacy Suit lore (last gift, defensive barrier) is from Retro design director Bill Vandervoort in the Nintendo Dream interview; its loss on planting the fruit is reported by Nintendo Life and a search snippet. 'Born one in tens of thousands with a forehead crystal' is from a fan-wiki snippet; content only says 'a rare few'. Fan etymology (lament + mourn) omitted.

entries.comment: Prime 4: Tanamaar and the Desolan System
entries.content:
Tanamaar is a rocky, barren planet with at least one moon in the Desolan System, occupied by the Galactic Federation and the site of the UTO Research Center. In Cosmic Year 20X9 Federation researchers there unearthed an alien artifact that their analysis could identify only as some kind of device. It was in truth a Lamorn return teleporter: one of the twelve Lamorn who left Viewros to search for a prophesied Chosen One had died on Tanamaar, and the Federation had found what it carried.

Sylux and his Space Pirates, who had been raiding Federation research facilities with mind-controlling Metroids, struck the UTO Research Center while Samus Aran was on reconnaissance nearby, and Federation HQ sent her to secure the artifact (Metroid Prime 4: Beyond). Her security ID gave her full access, and a trooper sent her off with "Go get 'em, Samus." Command ordered the artifact moved to the hangar and loaded onto a transport while Pirate breach charges tore through the gates and wounded Pirates and troopers lay in the corridors. In the hangar Samus destroyed Aberax, a Space Pirate officer fused with a Metroid, and then faced Sylux himself. His fire damaged the artifact; it activated and enveloped the whole center in an energy burst. Samus, Sylux, the engineer Myles MacKenzie, the soldiers Reger Tokabi, Ezra Duke and Nora Armstrong, the android VUE-995, the Federation MK-99 mech Betsy and chunks of the facility were all carried off to Viewros.

Debris from the UTO Research Center lies scattered across Viewros, and its salvaged mech parts and power cores became the raw material of the group's escape. Where the Master Teleporter finally delivered Samus is uncertain; she emerged on a barren, rocky world that may or may not have been Tanamaar.
entries.notes: Desolan System confirmed by Metroid Wiki's premise summary, the Shinesparkers transcript of the opening text and preview coverage. 'At least one moon, rocky and barren' comes from a Wikitroid snippet quoted in search results (lower confidence). The artifact as a Lamorn searcher's teleporter is supported by the Shinesparkers Lamorn feature, Tanabe's interview and a fan-wiki snippet. Samus's post-escape destination: one guide says Tanamaar, another a planet 'many think is Tanar', and a wiki notes the hologram does not match Tanamaar's moon; left uncertain.

entries.comment: Prime 4: Myles MacKenzie and the stranded Federation marines
entries.content:
When the Lamorn artifact on Tanamaar detonated, five members of the Galactic Federation garrison of the UTO Research Center were hurled to Viewros alongside Samus Aran (Metroid Prime 4: Beyond). Scattered across the planet, they sent out distress signals, and Samus found them one by one.

- Myles MacKenzie: a Federation engineering specialist who maintains and repairs vehicles and writes software for weapons development. Timid, rarely at the front and talkative even when alone, he is restlessly curious yet so cautious that it keeps him alive, with a strong moral compass and work ethic. Samus found him in Fury Green trapped in his wrecked transport amid Griever-infested vines; once freed he handed her the Missile Launcher stored aboard, restored comms and asked, "What do you say? Teammates?" Samus nodded. He set up the Base Camp in Fury Green, received salvaged mech parts there by teleporter patch, and rebuilt the shattered MK-99 Federation mech Betsy, which he had once worked on ("Poor Betsy…"), to batter down the barrier around the Chrono Tower.
- Reger Tokabi: a Federation sniper, a solitary hunter from a remote world who enlisted in search of a stable life. He always carries a tiger-shaped talisman he credits with his survival, and his family's faith in the god Sollan sits uneasily with his missions. He camped in Sol Valley, gave Samus a Teleporter Chip, and spoke to her about his upbringing and the sacred feel of the planet.
- Sergeant Ezra Duke: a veteran of countless engagements with the Space Pirates, stubborn and prone to clashing with superiors, but sincere, compassionate and dependable in a fight. Samus freed him from a generator in Flare Pool, and at Base Camp it was Duke who confirmed the final push on the tower.
- Private First Class Nora Armstrong: bright and proactive, with an intuitive command of structures and vehicles. She has admired Samus since they met, and her outbursts about her annoy her superiors. Samus met her on a tram in Flare Pool; "Finally, we get to go home," she said when the way out seemed open.
- VUE-995: a Federation combat android built to replace human pilots of fighters, armored vehicles and bipedal mechs, armed with shoulder missile launchers and sonic-boom emitters in its palms. It has no emotions but produces pseudo-emotions at times, and apologized for wrecking Betsy, the mech that punched through the barrier.

All five fought beside Samus against Sylux at the Pinnacle of the Chrono Tower, reviving one another and stripping away his shields. When Sylux returned and crippled the Master Teleporter they grabbed him and held him down so that Samus could escape; Tokabi threw her his tag as she went. Samus left them on Viewros and hung Tokabi's tag on the tree she grew from the Memory Fruit in their memory. Whether any of them survived is unknown.
entries.notes: Names and ranks verified across Nintendo Life (translating Nintendo's Japanese site), the in-game logbook (Omega Metroid), Wikipedia and GameSpot. Metroid Wiki spells 'Mackenzie'; most other sources 'MacKenzie'. The transcript gives his self-introduction as 'specialist Myles MacKenzie, Engineer Level 4' (rank wording omitted to avoid meta-sounding text). 'God Sollan' is from the logbook summary only. The object Tokabi throws is called a tag (Nintendo Life), a pendant (Wikipedia) or a good-luck charm (VGC). Armstrong's line is quoted by GameSpot without exact timing. One snippet says Tokabi was treated in a Lamorn healing pod after a fight in Sol Valley (single source, omitted). VUE-995's rescue location is unconfirmed.

entries.comment: Prime 4: The Chrono Tower and the Master Teleporter
entries.content:
The Chrono Tower is a vast tooth-shaped Lamorn structure floating above the desert of Sol Valley on Viewros. It served as the trial ground where a Chosen One would be certified, and its summit, the Pinnacle, houses the Master Teleporter together with Lamorn sleeping and healing pods. After the Great Tragedy the surviving Lamorn converted their Psy-bot servitor machines into anti-Griever soldiers that defend the tower and are launched from it in pods. Its halls include the Vestibule, the Guardian Chamber, the Statuary Hall, the Nexus of Hope and the Sanctum of the Guardians, where holograms record the Guardians of the keys.

The Master Teleporter grew from the priest Shei's insight into the structure of space and time; it was meant to carry the Lamorn legacy to a new world. Lekhash devised its sealing mechanism and the five Master Teleporter Keys, which the Lamorn entrusted to Guardians in each region of Viewros and hid in pocket dimensions reached through the Sacred Shrines. The teleporter answers only to one with psychic abilities who holds all five keys. Smaller return teleporters, such as the artifact unearthed on Tanamaar, were carried offworld by the twelve Lamorn who went searching for the Chosen One.

Samus Aran woke inside the tower after the Tanamaar explosion (Metroid Prime 4: Beyond). A Guardian mechanoid guided her to the Psychic Crystal, and at the Pinnacle a statue played the recording of Chatoyant Vooloon that named her the Chosen One and told her of the keys; a teleportation orb then carried her to Fury Green. Sylux, healing in one of the pods, later seized the tower, raised a barrier around it and used it to dispatch Psy-bot Mimics against her. With the keys gathered and the barrier broken by the Federation mech Betsy, Samus and her companions returned; at the Nexus of Hope a statue delivered Chatoya's final message, and at the Pinnacle Sylux attacked. After his defeat Samus set the keys and activated the Master Teleporter. Sylux returned and damaged it; it could hold open only briefly and worked only for her. While the five Federation soldiers pinned Sylux, Samus stepped through, the only one of the stranded to leave Viewros.
entries.notes: Tower purpose (trial site, activation device, sleeping pods, Psy-bot defenders) is from Nintendo's Japanese site via Omega Metroid's machine translation; Psy-bot conversion after the Great Tragedy is confirmed by the Machines logbook. Room names are from the ludo.guide finale walkthrough (single source). Keys hidden in an alternate dimension via Sacred Shrines: Technology logbook. 'Only someone with Psychic Abilities and all five keys' is a fan-wiki statement echoed by GameSpot's 'works only if Samus operates it'.

entries.comment: Prime 4: Grievers and the Guardians of the Keys
entries.content:
Grievers are the feral monsters that overran Viewros. They are not native beasts but transformed Lamorn: when the Lamorn showered their world with Green Energy to revive it, the energy reacted with the psychic crystals implanted in their people and twisted them into savage, mindless hunters. The Lamorn called this the Great Tragedy. Griever packs hunted the uncorrupted survivors, and the attempts to cure them in the Ice Belt laboratories only worsened the mutation (Metroid Prime 4: Beyond).

Varieties:
- Jungle Griever (Fury Green): thin-skinned pack hunters that leap and climb through the trees.
- Sand Griever (Sol Valley): ambushers that bury themselves in the dunes; packs rotate territories and merge to face great threats.
- Frostburn Griever (Ice Belt): pale specimens revived from the Lamorn cryopods, cold-resistant but weak to heat.
- Maul Griever and Maul Griever Brute (Great Mines): burrowers that hunt by sound and attack in waves; loud noises draw hordes. Brutes, swollen by excess Green Energy, spit mucus that hardens into barriers.
- Omega Griever: the largest and strongest Griever, apex predator of the Great Mines. It killed Gravinax, the eight-limbed, four-horned Guardian of the mines' Master Teleporter Key, and took its place and its key.

The Guardians of the keys were creatures and minds the Lamorn trusted; Sylux infused four of them with his Metroids:
- Carvex (Fury Green): a giant carnivorous plant that once communed telepathically with the priests, driven to attack everything.
- Xelios (Volt Forge): the organic-cell artificial intelligence that managed vehicle manufacturing, still following its last instructions until the fusion turned it into a battle AI.
- Keratos (Ice Belt): a one-of-a-kind armored giant with an iceberg-like shell, its mind and body irreversibly altered.
- Phenoros (Flare Pool): a huge mineral life-form in the lava lake of Magdrahda that feeds on Green Energy.

Other dangers include Varmis, a giant sand-swimming crustacean of Sol Valley grown enormous on Green Energy, Snow Wolves that hunt in ranked packs in the Ice Belt, and the Behemoth of Flare Pool, an armored arthropod whose four eyes are its only weakness. Samus Aran fought Grievers in every region of Viewros and destroyed each Guardian and the Omega Griever to claim the five keys; the Sanctum of the Guardians in the Chrono Tower preserves holographic records of them.
entries.notes: Creature lore is from the in-game Biology logbook as transcribed by Omega Metroid, cross-checked against walkthroughs (VGC, Omega Metroid boss guide) and Wikipedia's plot. Gravinax and 'Omega Griever took its place' come from Wikitroid snippets in search results plus the logbook's note that Omega Griever is not an assigned guardian (lower confidence on Gravinax's description). General Viewros fauna belongs to the bestiary-prime domain and is only touched on here.

entries.content:
The Vi-O-La is a Lamorn motorcycle that Samus Aran rode across Viewros (Metroid Prime 4: Beyond). Built in the Lamorn Machine Era as a two-wheeled single-seat vehicle and redesigned in the Psychic Era, it recognizes the brain waves of a registered rider, who alone can use it and can summon it from anywhere unless impassable terrain blocks its path. It was prototyped and tested at the Volt Forge factory, where Samus acquired it together with the Vi-O-La Suit that registers her as its rider. The machine boosts to ram through enemies and ore deposits, power-slides through turns and crowds, and launches energy orbs at up to five locked targets that return like boomerangs; it also draws Green Energy out of the Green Energy Crystals strewn across the desert. Fitted with the Vi-O-La IC Suit it enters IC mode, hovering over magma and lava, which let Samus cross the molten pools of Flare Pool.

Sol Valley is the sun-scorched desert at the heart of Viewros and the hub from which Fury Green, Volt Forge, the Ice Belt, Flare Pool and the Great Mines branch off; the Chrono Tower floats above it. A Lamorn cargo launcher in Fury Green delivers travelers into the valley. The priest Vahkuun built shrines across it filled with Mote-driven devices, and the Sacred Shrines open onto pocket dimensions where the Master Teleporter Keys were hidden; Lamorn statues conceal underground chambers. The Green Energy showers the Lamorn fired over the valley from Flare Pool left its crystals unusually common and its wildlife swollen: Sand Grievers ambush from the dunes, and Varmis, a giant crustacean that swims through sand, swallowed a power core from the wreckage of the UTO Research Center. Reger Tokabi made his camp here, marked by the smoke of his fire, and Samus hauled Federation debris and mech parts from the sands to rebuild the mech Betsy. Samus crossed the valley countless times, and it was on its sands that she first rode the Vi-O-La.
entries.notes: Vi-O-La lore (Machine Era origin, rider registration, remote summoning, IC mode) is from the in-game Technology logbook via Omega Metroid; Lamorn invention also confirmed by Nintendo's official site text. Features (boost, slide, five-target boomerang orbs) from Nintendo Wire summarizing Nintendo's Japanese site. 'Samus first rode it in Sol Valley' is inferred from Sol Valley being the hub where the bike is used; VGC says it is acquired in Volt Forge. The last sentence's 'countless times' is descriptive, not sourced.

entries.content:
Sylux's Metroids are a strain he bred from the Metroid hatchling he stole from a Federation research station after the Bermuda System incident. Exploiting the creature's imprinting, he cloned it and cultivated copies with a new ability: they fuse with a host organism and take control of its mind. With them he possessed Space Pirate officers, seized command of their army, and turned the Pirates against Galactic Federation research facilities in Cosmic Year 20X9 (Metroid Prime 4: Beyond). Federation intelligence already suspected that the raiders were being controlled by Metroids able to merge with other life-forms, and a fused host betrays itself by green-glowing growths.

Aberax was the first such host Samus Aran met: a huge beetle-like Space Pirate of command rank, nearly immune to beams and explosives and able to deploy a barrier. Metroid fusion stripped it of free will and grew up to four beam-projecting lenses in its chest; only destroying every lens forces it to vent its core energy. It dropped into the hangar of the UTO Research Center on Tanamaar as the artifact was being loaded for evacuation, and Samus destroyed it moments before Sylux himself arrived with more Pirates and Metroids.

On Viewros Sylux pushed the technique further, infusing his Metroids into the Lamorn Guardians of the Master Teleporter Keys. Carvex, Xelios, Keratos and Phenoros each lost the ability to communicate and attacked everything near them; the fusion left exposed, vulnerable tissue, and in Phenoros's case Samus had to pass down the creature's throat to reach the Metroid lodged deep inside it. Metroids flanked Sylux himself in the final battle at the Chrono Tower, and he still commands them on Viewros. For Samus, who has fought Metroids since Zebes and SR388 and once carried the baby Metroid that saved her, these mind-controlling hosts were a new kind of enemy, and a reminder that the hatchling Sylux stole might have been as gentle as the one she protected.
entries.notes: 'Sylux Metroid' as the variant name comes from Nintendo's Japanese site (machine-translated by Omega Metroid). Breeding/imprinting/Pirate-officer control is from Nintendo Today app text (Nintendo World Report) and a World Databook snippet; the in-game Sylux logbook says he cloned a stolen Metroid and used clones to control minds. Aberax details are from the in-game logbook (Omega Metroid) and the Shinesparkers transcript; Metroid Wiki's Aberax page is a stub. 'Green-glowing growths' is based on the Japanese-site note about Phenoros and the green weak points reported in Aberax/Sylux descriptions (moderate confidence). The last sentence's comparison is Samus-centered framing; the hatchling's temperament is not stated in canon. Abhorts are listed by Metroid Wiki as enemies but no description was found, so they are omitted.

result.research_notes:
Scope and sourcing: Metroid Prime 4: Beyond (released December 4, 2025, Switch and Switch 2) is thinly covered on Metroid Wiki: the main article, Sylux, Lamorn, Planet_Tanamaar, Aberax (stub), Delano_7 and Vi-O-La (stub) exist, but Viewros, Myles_MacKenzie/Mackenzie, Griever, Chrono_Tower, Fury_Green, Sol_Valley, Chatoyant_Vooloon, Legacy_Suit, UTO_Research_Center, Master_Teleporter_Key, Omega_Griever, Psychic_Abilities and the category page all returned 404. Wikitroid is blocked, as is its breezewiki mirror (Anubis bot wall); Game8 pages returned empty bodies; TV Tropes, GameFAQs, Neoseeker, Sportskeeda and GameSpot galleries returned 403. The GameSpot ending essay was read via its Yahoo syndication. Primary-text substitutes were the Shinesparkers transcript (opening text, UTO dialogue, MacKenzie lines) and Omega Metroid's transcriptions of the in-game Biology, Machines, Technology and Lamorn Legacy logbooks, plus Omega Metroid's translation of the Tanabe Nintendo Dream interview and its machine-translated summary of Nintendo's Japanese site. Wikitroid content reached me only as search-result snippets and is flagged as lower confidence where used.
